Figure 1: Skill-orchestration workflow: (a) teleoperated data collection,
(b) segmentation into motion primitives and learned skills, (c) execution, where
the learned skill acts after classical point-to-point motion.

Figure 2: (a) Before/after success of paired runs, both jigs, with
Fisher exact $p$ ; labels name every setting that differed. † Pick rate
of the grasp skill; other rows: insert rate of the grasp-then-insert pairing. (b) Pearson $r$ between offline metrics and the insert-given-pick rate,
one metric per cell within one policy group (centre-only or both-jig
checkpoints); coloured cells are reliable.

one metric per cell within one policy group (centre-only or both-jig
checkpoints); coloured cells are reliable.

Figure 3: Start positions ( $x$ , $y$ of the end effector in the robot base
frame) of the grasp episodes in the all-episode and balanced-200
sets, with their convex hulls. Stars mark the two test start positions. The
balanced set keeps the spread of start positions while evening out the
clusters formed by the jig placements.

Figure 4: Training loss (solid) and validation loss (dotted) of the deployed
skill of each policy family, from the runs’ training logs; each panel states
how often the validation loss was computed and the skill’s robot rate. In every
family the validation loss reaches its minimum early and is then flat or rising
while the training loss keeps falling, regardless of the robot rate
(36–100% insert-given-pick); $\pi_{0.5}$ finetuning uses no validation
split.
